## DF04 — Retire residual compatibility paths

- [ ] **Startup storage conversion.** At `bdaecaac`, `SqlGameRepository.load` in `apps/server/src/store.ts` still falls back from a missing canonical head to `world`/`world_journal`, reconstructs the old document, verifies retired knowledge/inner-world projections, writes canonical records and deletes the old rows in one transaction. `initialize` still creates those retired tables/projections. The schema-4 marker and current-world validator narrow admission but do not remove this older-layout conversion. Remove that compatibility path and its obsolete projection-only initialization through the existing repository owner; a nonempty incompatible database must be refused with its bytes intact, never mistaken for a fresh database or automatically reset. Preserve creation of an actually empty database, ordinary canonical reopen, complete current-format recovery, current forgetting/accounting and writer-conflict behavior. Trace all callers before removing shared code or tables; do not replace the fallback with another converter.
- [ ] **Unused converters and stale recovery guidance.** `upgradeObjects` and `upgradeAppraisals` remain exported from `packages/domain/src/index.ts`; repository source/scripts/tests have no callers beyond those exports at `bdaecaac`. Their old policy injection and conversion instructions contradict the [root policy](../../AGENTS.md#development-save-policy). Retire those compatibility-only exports/implementations, not the current object/appraisal owners. Audit the retained whole-JSON save and database recovery-payload branches for actual current callers before removing compatibility-only forms; preserve current format, checksum, size and pointer validation. The operational-backup error recommending a compatible older server must instead preserve the source and explain current support. [BW04](../limits/persistence.md#bw04), [SV14](../limits/persistence.md#sv14) and [SB17](../limits/persistence.md#sb17) document the observed boundaries.

**Exit:** source/caller review shows one current-format path and no automatic older-layout conversion or world-policy injection; relevant existing static and disposable PostgreSQL checks cover empty creation, canonical reopen, current-format save/restore, incompatible populated input refusal without mutation, uncertain commits and accounting/privacy continuity. This documentation pass records confirmed residual code and distinguishes unassessed compatibility-only callers; it does not claim deletion or new runtime qualification
